- Patient presents with sudden, severe, left-sided headache waking him from sleep (onset 5:30 am); photophobia present (mild); no neck stiffness, fever, or significant nausea/vomiting; Paracetamol not effective.
- History of milder frontal headaches, but new severe, unilateral nature.
- Ongoing work-related stress and poor sleep identified as possible contributing factors.
- DDx: Migraine (high likelihood; supported by unilateral pain, photophobia, and stress/sleep triggers); tension-type headache (moderate/medium likelihood; history of anxiety/stress, but current episode less typical—more severe/one-sided); secondary headache (e.g., mass, very low likelihood—warrants watchful waiting given new severe morning headache, but no neurological deficit or other red flags at present).
- No supporting evidence of infection, medication overuse, or other secondary causes.
- No abnormal neurological findings reported (telemedicine—no physical exam available).

Management Plan
- Start Ibuprofen for acute headache (dose/route/frequency not documented); Paracetamol may be continued.
- Advise increased hydration (1.5–2 L water daily, excluding caffeine).
- Recommend ensuring 7–8 hours sleep per night.
- Encourage stress reduction (consider time off work/self-certification; counseling/self-referral recommended—link to be provided).
- Follow-up in one week to reassess.
- Provide patient with written information on danger signs and when to seek urgent care.
- Advise to seek medical help if symptoms worsen.
- No investigations ordered at this stage; consider blood tests if symptoms persist.

- Migraine—High likelihood. Sudden/severe, one-sided headache with photophobia, stress and sleep deprivation as triggers, supported by current episode details.
- Tension-type headache—Moderate likelihood. History of stress/anxiety and previous headaches, but current phenotype less typical (more severe, one-sided).
- Secondary headache (e.g., intracranial mass)—Low likelihood. New severe morning headache, but no neurological deficits or vomiting; to be monitored.
